subject: Interim data routing certification and ops runbook
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@healthtechlabs.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>; Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@procurecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency: interim certification & evidence request

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our DPO has asked for a concrete interim plan that covers two things before signature: (1) an operations runbook that explains how Redwood will honour EU-region pinning and what temporary cross-region processing looks like for failover/replication, and (2) evidence we can share with our internal security review (subprocessor roster, sample telemetry showing egress alerts, and a draft DPA addendum).

Specific asks:
- Can you provide a short runbook describing the sequence when EU pinning cannot be met (failover / permitted windows, notification cadence, time-to-resolve)?
- Are you able to provide a current subprocessor roster and a short explanation of how you notify customers of new subprocessors?
- Will Redwood sign a DPA addendum that includes a temporary-evidence clause (e.g., 72-hour temporary egress for critical maintenance with prior notification)?
- Any KMS/HSM options for customer-managed keys we can point to in the review?

We need these artifacts by the end of next week to keep the contract on the current quarter. If you need to loop legal or ops, please do.

Best,
Sarah Lim
Chief Security Officer
HealthTech Labs

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency: interim certification & evidence request

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass runbook (redwood-residency-runbook-v1.pdf) and our subprocessor roster (subprocessor-roster-2027-03.csv). High-level summary here so your DPO can triage immediately:

1) EU region pinning:
- Default: requests from EU-region customers are served by EU-hosted instances and EU-local storage by default.
- Failure mode: if EU capacity is exhausted or there's an infrastructure incident, we have a controlled failover process that prefers EU-compatible cloud regions first. Emergency cross-region processing is time-limited and follows our notification & approval flow below.

2) Temporary cross-region processing (proposal):
- We propose a 72-hour temporary egress window for critical failover/maintenance with 24-hour prior notice when possible. If an emergency prevents notice, we will open a post-event incident briefing and provide audit logs within 48 hours.

3) DPA addendum:
- Draft attached (dpa-addendum-draft.docx). It captures temporary egress windows, required notification cadence, and an explicit attestation clause for subprocessors. Legal will need to review and sign.

4) KMS options:
- We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or GCP Cloud KMS in our Private deployment. For Hosted customers we offer a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) option with HSM-backed wrapping for EU-only keys on an add-on.

Next steps / who I'm looping: Marissa (legal ops) and Laura (privacy & compliance) are cc'd to confirm acceptance criteria for the DPA language and evidence. Karthik — can you confirm the telemetry sample we can share (ops-telemetry-sample.json) and whether the current logging exports will show the exact egress timestamps the DPO will want?

I'll follow up with a short canary plan and Ops runbook summary if this mapping looks right.

Thanks,
Avery
Director, Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Mar 22, 2027 at 10:40 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
>
> 2) Temporary cross-region processing (proposal):
> - We propose a 72-hour temporary egress window for critical failover/maintenance with 24-hour prior notice when possible. If an emergency prevents notice, we will open a post-event incident briefing and provide audit logs within 48 hours.
>
Agree with that approach, with the following edits before we share externally:
- Replace generic "72-hour" language with "up to 72 hours for transient processing unless otherwise agreed in writing" so we have explicit carve-outs for longer repairs that need contract-level escalation.
- Add an SLA-exception workflow: customer notifies Redwood account lead; Redwood creates an internal incident with priority and notifies customer within 1 hour of classification.
- For KMS: confirm that hosted BYOK is opt-in and will require a short onboarding window (we should include an expected time-to-enable in the runbook).

Karthik — can ops confirm the telemetry sample is safe to share (redact IPs) and includes: egress timestamp, affected model/version, route taken (region ids), and incident id? If yes, attach with redaction.

Laura — legal suggested one additional audit clause in the DPA addendum giving the customer a right to request a one-time SOC2 artifact review for residency controls on sign-off. Thoughts?

I'll prepare a consolidated runbook and DPA edit and send back to Avery for customer-facing copy.

Marissa
Head, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Oliver —

Appreciate the patience while we consolidated internal reviews. Attached are the materials we discussed and the proposed next steps to keep procurement on track:

What we're attaching (for your review):
- redwood-residency-runbook-v1.pdf — operations runbook with incident classification, notification flow, and failover sequencing.
- subprocessor-roster-2027-03.csv — current list of subprocessors (PII redacted where relevant).
- ops-telemetry-sample.json — redacted telemetry showing an example egress event, timestamps, and region routing.
- dpa-addendum-draft.docx — draft addendum with temporary egress language and a one-time SOC2 artifact review clause (per Marissa's suggestion).

Key commitments (summary):
- Default hosting: EU-region pinned for EU customers.
- Temporary cross-region processing: up to 72 hours for transient failover/maintenance unless otherwise agreed in writing; emergency events will be followed by an incident briefing and logs within 48 hours.
- Notification: 24-hour prior notice for planned maintenance; 1-hour initial acknowledgement for classified incidents.
- KMS: BYOK options are available for Private deployments; Hosted BYOK is opt-in and requires an onboarding lead time (we've documented expected enablement timelines in the runbook).
- Audit evidence: we will provide the listed artifacts and support a one-time SOC2 artifact review as part of DPA execution.

Requested next steps:
1) Please review the attached runbook & DPA draft and share any redlines by EOD Friday (2027-04-02).
2) If the DPA addendum language is acceptable, we will send the DocuSign envelope for signature (link below).
3) Once signed, ops will schedule a short onboarding call to review BYOK options and the incident playbook.

DocuSign (proposed): https://www.docusign.com/HTL-Residency-Addendum
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/HTL-DEAL-7831

If you want a short walkthrough of the runbook we can schedule a 30-minute slot this week — I can bring Karthik for the telemetry pieces and Laura for legal Qs.

Thanks,
